text.zh: 嚴兵扼守海口，而以兵艦往搗之，攻其不備，否則載勁旅抵朝鮮東偏釜山鎮等處，深溝高壘，絕其歸路，分兵徇朝鮮諸郡邑，彼進則迎擊，彼退則尾追，又出偏師撓之。彼糧盡援竭，人無鬥志，必土崩瓦解，此俄羅斯破法蘭西之計也。
text.en: hold the harbor mouth with strong forces and send warships to strike where the enemy is unprepared; or else land crack troops on Korea's eastern coast at Busan, entrench deeply, cut off their retreat, and spread forces through the Korean countryside—meet them when they advance, pursue when they retreat, and send flanking columns to harass them. When their supplies run out and reinforcements fail, their men will lose heart and collapse—this is how Russia broke France.

translationRepairs: In the twentieth year (1840), angered that Imperial Commissioner Lin Zexu was enforcing the opium ban in Guangdong and Guangxi, Britain sent warships to the Ningbo coast, captured Dinghai, and soon withdrew.

In the twentieth year (1840), because Imperial Commissioner Lin Zexu was firmly enforcing the opium ban in Guangdong and Guangxi, Britain displayed force off the Ningbo coast, captured Dinghai, and soon withdrew.
Chinese 以 marks cause (because Lin enforced the ban), not Britain's anger; 耀兵 is 'displayed force', not 'sent warships'.

In that campaign the dead at Dabaoshan in Cixi included acting magistrate Yan Lujing, brigade colonel Huang Tai, garrison commanders Tian Xi, Chen Zhilan, Xu Huan, and Hakelie, majors A Benrang and Wei Qiming, captains Lin Huaiyu, Lu Bing, and Di Fade, and staff officers Zhang Huapeng, Ma Longtu, He Hai, Mao Yugui, Wang Baoyuan, and Yang Fuzeng;

In that campaign the dead at Dabaoshan in Cixi included magistrate designated for immediate appointment Yan Lujing, brigade colonel Huang Tai, garrison commanders Tian Xi, Chen Zhilan, Xu Huan, and Hakelie, majors A Benrang and Wei Qiming, captains Lin Huaiyu, Lu Bing, and Di Fade, and staff officers Zhang Huapeng, Ma Longtu, He Hai, Mao Yugui, Wang Baoyuan, and Yang Fuzeng;
即用知縣 is a magistrate awaiting immediate substantive appointment, not an acting (署/權) magistrate.
His son Renhou inherited his office and later died fighting the Taiping rebels in Guangdong.
His son Renhou inherited his office and later died fighting the Guangdong rebels.
粵寇 is 'Guangdong rebels/bandits'; the idiomatic rendering names the Taiping, which the Chinese does not.

He rose from the ranks in campaigns against bandits in Huaxian; bold and resourceful, he once said, "On the battlefield a soldier puts life and death aside; anyone who fears death has no business wearing a sword."

He rose from the ranks in campaigns against bandits in Huaxian; bold and resourceful, he once said, "When a military officer faces battle, life and death are outside consideration; one who fears death should not be a military officer."
The closing clause is 不作武官矣 ('should not be a military officer'), not the invented 'wearing a sword'.
He entered service through the military examinations, joined the naval forces, and rose to captain.
From a military youth he joined the naval forces and rose to captain.
武童 is a military-youth recruit, not someone who 'entered service through the military examinations'.
Commander Ding Ruchang commanded from the Dingyuan but was paralyzed by fear, was wounded, and regional commander Liu Buchan took over.
Commander Ding Ruchang sat on the Dingyuan as flagship; he was timid and did not know what to do, was also wounded, and regional commander Liu Buchan replaced him.
Chinese 坐定遠督船 is 'sat on the Dingyuan as the flagship', not a generic 'commanded from'; 畏葸不知所為 is timidity, which the idiomatic 'paralyzed by fear' slightly overstates.
